adds.title: Recent killings of trans women prompt groups to push for LGBTQIA protection (Bulatlat)
adds.summary: Bulatlat, 26 June 2025, reports that 18-year-old trans woman Kierra Apostol (formerly Gian Molina), a business management student at Cagayan State University resident in Zone 7, Centro, Peñablanca, Cagayan, was found dead in a Cagayan province river on 23 June 2025, days after being reported missing; her mother told local media (95.7 XFM Tuguegarao) she saw visible signs of physical assault when the body was found. A criminology student of the University of Cagayan Valley, named online as 'Menco de Guzman'/'Sherwin Kyqle', voluntarily surrendered to the Peñablanca police station, admitting he picked Kierra up on Saturday night but denying involvement. Bahaghari chairperson Reyna Valmores Salinas called the killing proof that LGBTQ+ persons remain unsafe and renewed the call for the SOGIESC Equality Bill (House Bill No. 5551; Senate Bill No. 1600), noting no national anti-discrimination law has passed in 25 years. Documents a second trans-woman killing inside Cagayan Valley (Cagayan province) within the 2024-2025 national series this record tracks, with an identified suspect who surrendered to police.

adds.title: LGBTQIA+ groups, umalma sa ikalawang tala ng pamamaslang sa estudyanteng trans woman (Manila Today)
adds.summary: Manila Today, 25 June 2025 (Filipino), reports that two days after Kierra Apostol was reported missing, the trans woman student — an incoming first-year Business Management student at Cagayan State University-Caritan Campus and a hair-and-makeup artist active in local gay pageants — was found floating in the river between Amulung and Iguig in Cagayan on the morning of 23 June 2025, her mother citing marks of violence. LGBTQIA+ groups including CSU Crystal (Cagayan State University-Andrew campus), LGBT Pilipinas Taguig City Inc. and Bahaghari chair Reyna Valmores Salinas demanded a full and thorough investigation, justice, and immediate passage of the SOGIESC Equality Bill. Independent corroboration of the second documented trans-woman killing in this region, adding the Amulung-Iguig river location and the suspect-surrender detail beyond the Bulatlat account.

adds.title: Trans woman makes history as she graduates summa cum laude from Capiz State U (Inquirer.net)
adds.summary: Inquirer.net, 7 August 2025, reports that at its 21st commencement exercises Capiz State University produced its first openly trans woman to graduate summa cum laude — Khaz-JP Padilla, batch valedictorian of the social work class with the highest Latin honor — the outcome this record attributes to the Capiz State advocacy campaign that followed the October 2022 hair-and-uniform directive. Padilla describes the school's binary haircut rules she faced in earlier years ('Why is it that whenever I cut my hair... it feels like I'm losing my self-confidence?') and her transition once pandemic-era online classes freed her from the haircut rule. Confirms the 'first openly trans woman graduating as valedictorian with highest honours' milestone claimed in the record. Page verified via a Wayback Machine snapshot of 5 January 2026; the live Inquirer.net URL is Cloudflare-gated.

adds.title: Municipal Ordinance No. 15, Series of 2023, Municipality of Bayambang, Pangasinan — An Ordinance Protecting the Rights of Lesbians, Gays, Bisexuals, Transgenders, Queers and Intersex (LGBTQI) in the Municipality of Bayambang Against Any and All Forms of Discrimination Solely on the Basis of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Expression, Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC) and Providing Penalties for Violation Thereof (certified copy)
adds.summary: The certified eight-page copy of Bayambang Municipal Ordinance No. 15, s-2023, authored by Coun. Benjamin Francisco S. De Vera, protects LGBTQI persons in the municipality against discrimination 'solely on the basis of sexual orientation, gender identity, expression, sex characteristics (SOGIESC)' and sets a penalty ladder: first offence a fine of at least Php1,000 or one month's imprisonment; second offence at least Php2,000 or one month-and-a-day to six months; third offence at least Php2,500 or six months-and-a-day to eight months; later violations one year's imprisonment plus at least Php2,500; violators must also complete mandatory human rights education. Complaints are filed through the barangay (Katarungang Pambarangay) mechanism under R.A. 7160, giving a visitor in the Pangasinan corridor an actual local complaint route. This is the operative municipal instrument endorsed provincially by the Pangasinan Provincial Board Resolution No. 799-2024 cited in the record's existing source.

adds.title: Municipal Ordinances — Municipality of Bayambang (official registry of the Sangguniang Bayan)
adds.summary: The official registry of the Municipality of Bayambang lists Ordinance No. 15-2023, 'An Ordinance Protecting the Rights of Lesbians, Gays, Bisexuals, Transgenders, Queers and Intersex (LGBTQI) in the Municipality of Bayambang Against Any and All Forms of Discrimination Solely on the Basis of Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity, Expression, Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC) and Providing Penalties for Violation Thereof,' as authored by Hon. Benjamin Francisco S. De Vera and dated October 16, 2023, with a public View page that hosts the certified PDF copy. Confirms the number, series, author and enactment date this record cites for Bayambang's local protective ordinance.
